IN JANUARY last year, Jyoti Maan's baby was bom premature at week 29, weighing a mere 780 grams. As the newborn battled it out for nine months in the neonatal ICU of AIIMS, Delhi, Jyoti, lactating and separated from her baby, donated nearly 25 litres of her breast milkto the new milk bank

at AIIMS. While Jyoti lost her baby at the end of those traumatic nine months, she ended up being alifesaver for nearty 30 newboms. Jyoti says that when her baby was bom, he was put on ventilator support and needed very littleofher milk. "As was lactating, the nurses from the AIIMS milk bank asked meif I could give my excess milk to other babies who needed it. Since my baby didn't need so much milk, decided to helpothermothers instead of lettingit go waste," she says. Payodhi, the milk bank at Al-IMS that was inaugurated in

February, reliesondonor mothers like Jyoti for the pre-term babies - those born before 32 weeks or weighing less than 1.5 kg - under itscare. Setupas part of the Health Ministry's guide-lines to open more lactation management centres, the facility at AIIMS is the second breast milk bank ina public hospitalin Delhi and one of only 90 such centres across the country. Doctors and public health specialists say milk banks can play a key role in reducing neonatal deaths - in India, an estimated 5.8 lakh newboms die CONTINUEDON PAGE2
